New Mexico protected a lead in the defensive Havoc department, as Virginia Tech took a step back in a loss to Clemson, while Tennessee and Louisiana Tech continue to climb on the defensive side of the ball. The safest offense in the nation continues to be Notre Dame after a big win over Miami. college football-picks-havoc rankings-week 11 For those unfamiliar, Havoc is the collection of stats that can derail offensive momentum on the defensive side of the ball, including tackles for loss, pass breakups, forced fumbles, interceptions, and sacks. Havoc allowed, meanwhile, is a stat used to quantify an offense's ability to avoid chaos that creates a negative play. Offenses that are elite in Havoc allowed have a low number of fumbles, interceptions, and tackles for loss allowed. Let's take a look at our college football picks for Illinois vs. UCLA and Week 11 Havoc Rankings for the upcoming week. away.blurb: "We can't look ahead. We can't listen to anybody tell us we're good, or we're bad, or whatever it might be," Chesney said. "We just have to take a deep dive and self-evaluate on a day-to-day basis and figure out: How can we get better?" UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach says first-half shoulder injury vs. Illinois not serious - ABC7 Los Angeles 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California SPORTS Share PASADENA, Calif. -- UCLA starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach exited just before halftime because of a shoulder injury Friday but returned in the third quarter to lead the No. 4 Bruins past Illinois 22-14 for their 10th win of the season, tying a program record last reached in 1998. With 35 seconds left in the first half and the Bruins driving, Dieffenbach was tackled after throwing the ball downfield and appeared to land awkwardly. After being examined by trainers, he stood and gingerly walked off the field with the help of two teammates. "I went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up," said Dieffenbach, who is also nursing an ankle injury. "It just got tight. It's nothing serious." Coach Bob Chesney confirmed that Dieffenbach's injury wasn't serious and said he landed awkwardly on his non-throwing arm and hurt his elbow. "At halftime, his shoes are off, and he's got no shoulder pads. I'm like, 'Yeah, get your shoes back on,'" Chesney said. "But we had to go make sure everything was good in there and he was ready to go." The former Cal Poly quarterback, who took over after Week 1 starter Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending injury against Oregon last month, has led UCLA to five wins in five starts and has thrown for 1,218 yards and eight touchdowns. On Friday, he had thrown for 168 yards and a touchdown before he was replaced by third-stringer Madden Iamaleava , Nico's brother. Madden Iamaleava had one pass attempt all season and went 0-for-2 before the first half ended. The Bruins led the Illini 10-0 at the time. In the second half, with Dieffenbach still being evaluated, Madden Iamaleava led two drives that ended in a punt and a turnover on downs. By the time Dieffenbach emerged from the locker room to a loud ovation, UCLA was only up 12-7. "One of the best moments of my life hearing that crowd," Dieffenbach said. Numbers vary across the market, with BetMGM, DraftKings and Caesars currently showing Michigan +5.5, while FanDuel has Michigan +6.5. That number is smaller than Saturday’s game at Oregon, where the Wolverines opened as nearly two-touchdown underdogs before closing as 10-point underdogs. Michigan (5-5, 2-5 Big Ten) has failed to cover the spread in three straight games and six of its last seven, another sign of struggle for Kyle Whittingham’s team. As things stand currently, oddsmakers have also set a season-low point total for Saturday’s game, with books ranging from 37.5 to 39.5. The Bruins held off Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night to stay unbeaten, but it was the first time all season they failed to cover the spread. home.headline: UCLA endures injury scare, gets heroic return to stay unbeaten
home.blurb: It was a heroic return for the veteran who had departed UCLA’s game against Illinois just before halftime with a sore elbow and ankle. The crowd serenaded Dieffenbach with cheers anew once he came onto the field with his team holding a suddenly precarious lead over Illinois. All Dieffenbach did upon his return was to complete each of his five passes on the next drive, including a beautiful touchdown toss, to help the fourth-ranked Bruins hold on for a 22-14 victory that kept their unbeaten record intact. “That’s leadership, that stands out,” Chesney said, “and there’s the confidence everybody gained from that.” Illinois closed to within 19-14 after quarterback Katin Houser converted a huge fourth-down play, finding wide receiver Collin Dixon in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown with 7:14 left. But the Fighting Illini could conjure no more late magic after Houser went out with his own injury. “When we walked out there, I was like, damn, yes,” Chesney said of the crowd. “I knew we were on the brink of it and you were worried about the weather, but ultimately what a great job by them and really proud of the way they showed up.” After taking a shot in the arm, Ty Dieffenbach delivered one. Roars accompanied the previously injured UCLA quarterback with each step he took as he jogged back from the locker room to the Rose Bowl sideline late in the third quarter Friday night. “That crowd reaction was unbelievable,” Dieffenbach would say later. “I mean, that was one of the best moments of my life.” “They just don’t give up, they just don’t,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said of his players. “They just believe they have a shot to win every game and they’re going to find a way.” The Bruins could exhale only after an Illinois pass fell incomplete over the middle with 43 seconds left. UCLA had registered another big defensive play only minutes earlier when safety Scooter Jackson came up with an interception – his second of the game – and returned it 41 yards to the Illinois 19-yard line with 2 minutes 42 seconds left. A short Mateen Bhaghani field goal gave the Bruins a 22-14 lead, necessitating a desperation drive by the Fighting Illini that came up well short. There were feel-good vibes all around after Dieffenbach escaped injury and UCLA improved to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 – the last season it won a conference championship. “No one believed that UCLA would be 10-0 this year, no one in the country, no one anywhere,” linebacker Sammy Omosigho said, “and we had to make them believe.” The Bruins, who are 7-0 in Big Ten games, need only one more victory in their final two regular-season games – against Michigan and USC – to clinch an appearance in the conference title game. Among other things, a season-high crowd of 45,800 celebrated a UCLA defense that intercepted three passes and registered five tackles for loss while holding the Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3) to 240 yards of offense. SMU vs. No. 13 Wake Forest game preview
2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 16, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. picks.blurb: Wake Forest enters the game with an 8-1 record, while SMU is 7-2. The game has significant implications for the ACC championship race. Betting odds slightly favor SMU, but the prediction favors Wake Forest in a high-scoring game. Week 11 of the College Football season gets us closer to the precipice of championship weekend. The ACC has a great slate to end the season, and Week 11 features a ton of awesome games. The showstopper is on at Noon ET, with the Wake Forest Demon Deacons taking on the SMU Mustangs. Wake Forest (8-1) has looked the part of a championship contender. There aren't a ton of takeaways from their 76-0 win against Merrimack out of the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS), but it continues a trend of dominance for them. The Demon Deacons. They haven't been within one score of a team since their upset win against Louisville earlier in the season, winning by 20+ in all of the past five matchups and 40+ in three of their past five matchups. SMU (7-2) should be closer to the ACC championship than they are. They proved it with a dominating 51-28 win against then 6-2 Virginia Tech, where their offense scored on nine of their 11 possessions. However, they dropped an easy game against Syracuse on Halloween. They lost 30-27, giving up a last-minute touchdown drive. That's been the only holdup preventing them from being in Wake Forest's spot. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Here are the latest odds for the game, courtesy of BetMGM. Wake Forest vs. SMU game odds All college football odds via BetMGM Money Line: SMU -115, Wake Forest -105 Over/Under: Over 60.5 (-110), Under 60.5 (-110) Spread: SMU -1.5 (-105), Wake Forest +1.5 (-115) Wake Forest vs. SMU prediction, pick This might be the matchup with the most stakes in the ACC championship picture. If Wake Forest wins, they'll be 6-1 in the ACC and have tiebreakers over SMU and Louisville in the race, but if SMU wins, they'll be 6-2 in the ACC with one more game against Stanford remaining. If anyone's expecting the 13-12 defensive bout we got last year, throw that out the window. This should be a shootout. Both teams possess some of the best quarterbacks in the nation, with Gio Lopez and Kevin Jennings combining for 4,940 yards, 43 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. They're the biggest reason why either team is at the place it is now. Wake Forest has a few advantages, though. The Demon Deacons are one of the top teams in the nation at stopping the run, allowing just 82.9 yards per game (No. 5 in the country). The Mustangs are slightly above average against the run (133.9 yards per game, No. 45). The Demon Deacons are also favorites in the turnover battle. They're one of the most turnover-averse teams in the country (0.4 giveaways per game, No. 2 in the country), while the Mustangs are pretty turnover-prone (1.5 giveaways per game, No. 95). This game should have no problem hitting the over, with both of these teams boasting some of the top passing offenses in the league. However, give me the Demon Deacons in a road win. The Tennessee Vols head to College Station this weekend for a showdown with the Texas A&M Aggies. Despite being 4-5, A&M isn't playing terrible football, competing with both Alabama and South Carolina in recent weeks on the road. Tennessee comes in at No. 8 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, and they control their own path to almost certainly a home playoff game if they can take care of business. Will they start on the right foot at Kyle Field on Saturday? Our college football writers weighed in with their predictions. Tennessee 23, Texas A&M 16 This has been a game that, from an upset perspective, is more of a concern to me than the Kentucky game was. Tennessee is a different animal on the road in SEC play than they are at home under Josh Heupel. Pre-snap mistakes and head-scratching moments seem to happen more away from home, and despite Texas A&M being 4-5, Kyle Field will likely still be loud and rocking on Saturday. Tennessee has a 53% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 3% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 11, 2026). I still think Tennessee is in good position to win here based on their line play on both sides of the ball, although the loss of Tyree Weathersby stings. But Tennessee's ground game and physical defense proves to be enough to get out of town with a tough win and set up a de facto playoff game for them against LSU next week. Craig Smith , A to Z Sports Tennessee Tennessee 27, Texas A&M 10 This Tennessee defense is playing lights-out. One of the best in the country. And after putting up 450 yards of total offense last week, A&M still managed just nine total points vs. South Carolina. Their offense has been bad, and the defense hasn't been great, either. Tennessee will use this game to find a bit of a spark in the passing game and continue running the ball well. Justin Churchill , A to Z Sports Oklahoma Tennessee 30, Texas A&M 17 There are no down weeks in the SEC, even if Texas A&M is having a down year. For the Vols, this is a bit of a trap game. The Aggies are not what many predicted based on preseason rankings, and the matchup with LSU next week could very well be for a CFP spot when all is said and done. But it won't matter if Tennessee doesn't take care of business this week. The Vols have the two things that travel and make a good football team however: a run game and good trench play. I expect Tennessee to overpower the Aggies and get out with a victory ahead of a monumental matchup next week. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Tennessee 31, Texas A&M 14 Tennessee has its top-10 spot and will cruise into the College Football Playoff if it can avoid another loss. Texas A&M has been reeling badly, losing three of its last four games, and will fall to 4-6 following Week 11. The Vols are going to get the job done on the road, avoiding a potential upset ahead of a big game against LSU next weekend. This Tennessee defense is bad news for the Aggies' offense, and it could be a long day as a result. Brandon Little , A to Z Sports Ohio State Tennessee 28, Texas A&M 17 I expect Tennessee to have a tougher time early than some might anticipate. The Vols could come out a little sluggish offensively, allowing Texas A&M to hang around and potentially control portions of the first half. However, Tennessee has enough talent and offensive firepower to eventually find its rhythm. I like the Vols to make some adjustments at halftime, get the running game going, and put more pressure on the Aggies defense as the game progresses. The biggest difference comes down to quarterback play. Marcel Reed continues to have issues taking care of the football, and those mistakes are particularly costly against a Tennessee team that can turn turnovers into points quickly. The Aggies make a few plays to stay competitive, but they give Tennessee too many extra opportunities. The Vols take control in the second half, pull away late, and come away with an important SEC victory. The Volunteers are in a good spot inside the top-10 of the College Football Playoff rankings with a fantastic run game. The only thing that will keep the Aggies in the game is their run defense and Marcel Reed scrambling BS. I don't think the Volunteers defense will let him gash them. away.blurb: Kicker Cooper Ranvier was crucial, successfully making all five of his field-goal attempts. The Vols' defense held the Aggies to only one touchdown and secured two fourth-quarter interceptions. Getting to Texas A&M wasn’t easy for Tennessee football . Getting a crucial victory was even harder at times. As unlikely as success sometimes seemed in the first half, the Vols pulled it off in a 22-7 victory at Kyle Field on Nov. 14. Tennessee was off schedule from the start. It didn’t leave Knoxville until the night before the game after the FAA ordered a nationwide emergency ground stop Nov. 13 just before 4 p.m. for all departing flights. Tennessee’s troubles didn’t end with the travel delay. Its usually reliable running game slowed against the Texas A&M defense. Injuries mounted. But the No. 9 Vols persevered in boosting their record to 8-2 as they continued their drive to the College Football Playoff. Their drive had a noticeable limp against the Aggies, who fell to 4-6 with their sixth loss in seven SEC games. Mike Matthews, Tennessee’s leading receiver, incurred what appeared to be a serious knee injury in the first half. Quarterback George MacIntyre was sidelined by a knee injury in the third quarter. And the Vols already were without sack leader Tyree Weathersby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury a week earlier. Never mind the attrition. Tennessee again demonstrated its resilience and resourcefulness. Freshman Faizon Brandon, who began the season as Tennessee’s starting quarterback, threw one pass in relief of MacIntyre. But he made it count. His 5-yard pass to tight end DaSaahn Brame accounted for UT’s only touchdown. That fourth-quarter score put the Vols up 16-7. A nine-point lead in this defense-dominated matchup was insurmountable for the Aggies, who made only five first downs until the 5:30 mark of the fourth quarter. Their offense peaked early when freshman K J Edwards ran 25 yards for a touchdown. Tennessee’s defense never faltered after that. Once the Aggies were forced to play catchup, their offensive shortcomings were magnified. Texas A&M’s defense deserved a better fate. A Tennessee running game that was averaging 216 yards per game produced only 196 yards against the Aggies, who made UT star running back DeSean Bishop fight for every yard. Bishop, who had averaged 149.5 yards rushing in his last five games, was held to 97 yards on 34 carries. The Aggies defense was at its best when the Vols were closing in on its goal line. Aside from Brandon’s touchdown pass, Tennessee had to settle for field goals on every scoring drive. Cooper Ranvier came through each time. Despite a tricky wind, he made all five of his attempts. Ranvier, who transferred from Louisville, has proved to be a huge plus for Tennessee’s offense. He has made 18-of-19 field goals and hasn’t missed an extra-point attempt. home.blurb: Hobbs had recorded 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss in eight games prior to the injury. The Vols are facing depth issues on the defensive line, having already lost Tyree Weathersby for the season. Tennessee football defensive lineman Daevin Hobbs went to the medical tent midway through the first half of its game at Texas A&M on Nov. 14, but returned to the lineup for the second half. Hobbs limped off the field under his own power during Texas A&M's first drive of the second quarter. He went to the medical tent to be examined by athletic training staff. But he was on the field for Tennessee's first defensive series after halftime. The No. 9 Vols trailed Texas A&M 7-6 when Hobbs left the game. Going into the Texas A&M game, Hobbs had logged 12 total tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 4 quarterback hits in eight appearances. He made one tackle before exiting the game vs. the Aggies. Depth along the defensive line is becoming an issue for the Vols, who already lost Tyree Weathersby , the team leader in sacks with seven, to a season ending knee injury in the win over Kentucky on Nov. 7. However, during the Vols' 22-7 win at Texas A&M on Saturday, MacIntyre got banged up. He returned to the game for a drive after a knee injury, but returned to the injury tent afterward. Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel decided that Brandon gave his team the best chance to win going forward, given the health of MacIntyre and the need to pick up yardage on the ground. As a result, Brandon played the rest of the way. Now, the Vols have a quarterback controversy back on their hands. Tennessee will have to decide if it wants to go back to MacIntyre against LSU at home next week or keep the ball in Brandon's hands. MacIntyre's injury doesn't seem to have any long-term effect on that decision, either. According to a report from Pete Nakos, MacIntyre is not expected to miss any time with the knee injury. “George got twisted up on the one pass play,” Heupel said after the game. “And comes back in and was battling through it, but had to go back. And just with where the game was and what we felt like we needed, I didn’t feel like it was the right place for George, just dealing with that injury. And so that’s why Faizon was in there at that time. And both of them played extremely well. Proud of both of those guys, big smiles on their faces, excited about the win. They care about the team and straining and competing. So proud of them both.” Somewhat surprisingly, though, Vegas has Tennessee as the betting underdog at home. FanDuel lists LSU as 1.5-point favorites in the matchup at Neyland Stadium. You can get the Tigers at -115 and the Vols at -104 on the moneyline. The over/under point total for the game is set at 46.5 combined points scored. This means Vegas projects the game to finish in the ballpark of 24-22 in favor of LSU. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. Where to watch USC vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. USC vs. Indiana prediction, picks Five of Indiana's six Big Ten games have been decided by a touchdown or less. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. The Trojans have a veteran quarterback in Jayden Maiava who can keep his team in the game. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:37 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just when it seemed like USC was finished, and a new era would soon start with Lincoln Riley all but gone after an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin, a funny thing happened – the Trojans rolled Ohio State 30-18. And now, at 7-2, with high-profile dates remaining against CFP No. 9 Indiana and No. 8 UCLA, No. 18 USC all but controls its own path to the CFP – a 10-2 Trojan team with two top-ten wins in the final three games wouldn't be a lock to get in, but … yeah, it would be. But Indiana is still pretty good. It's 8-1, this close to being 9-0, and even though the schedule hasn't been a killer, if it keeps winning, all will be just fine. But lose this, and the pressure will be on to avoid a slip over the last two weeks. USC vs Indiana: Quick Hits Indiana travels to Washington after this before finishing with the rivalry date against Purdue. USC hosts Maryland after this before the showdown at UCLA. It's just the fifth meeting ever, and the first since USC joined the Big Ten. The Trojans are 4-0, including the 1968 Rose Bowl. How To Watch USC vs Indiana Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why USC Will Win Plenty of things have to go right. USC has the punting to own the field position game, there can't be a slew of turnovers, and Indiana has to keep struggling. The only way to put it is that it's like the Hoosiers forgot how to score. The offense is moving a bit, but it hasn't scored more than 20 points in regulation since early October. The USC passing game continues to be good enough. The ground game might be hit-or-miss, but Jayden Maiava is a smart, tough veteran who keeps hitting his throws for the Big Ten's best offense on third downs. Why Indiana Will Win Indiana got a week off to reset at just the right time. No, it's not playing nearly as well offensively as it did last year. No, it doesn't have that dominant mode, and it certainly doesn't have the same passing game. And yet it's still 8-1 – this bunch finds ways to win. For all of the issues on offense, the defense continues to be outstanding. The run D is the fourth-best in the nation, allowing just 2.3 yards per carry overall with no touchdowns in the last three games. USC might throw well, but it wasn't all that long ago that the ground game was stuffed for -18 yards by Wisconsin. USC vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Is Grant Wilson up to the gig, or will Josh Hoover get the nod as he fights through an injury? No matter who ends up under center, he'll be fine against a USC defense that's been hit hard by injuries. Indiana's offense – even without banged up star RB Turbo Richard – will be a bit more effective than it was against Ohio State, Michigan, or Minnesota, but it'll be the defensive front and run defense that keeps the good season going. away.blurb: Heading into Week 11 against USC, Indiana has several big names that are currently listed on the Big Ten availability report . The Ducks went into Columbus last week and crushed Ohio State, 41-28, to keep their languishing College Football Playoff hopes alive. Meanwhile, Michigan enters off a disgraceful performance at home against injury riddled rival Michigan State, punked 15-6 as a two-touchdown favorite. Who will get the last laugh on the field at Autzen Stadium? Michigan vs Oregon predictions Kyle Whittingham's first season at Michigan has been a disaster. The latest ignominy suffered by the Wolverines was an embarrassing loss to their undermanned in-state rival, Michigan State . It's hard to imagine U-M getting back up off the mat after absorbing that devastating blow and having the strength to grapple with a surging Oregon team on its home turf. Two-thousand miles away from Ann Arbor, expect the Wolverines to go down hard once again. The pick: Oregon 30, Michigan 7. In this battle of big-time NIL money, Phil Knight and Nike vs. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and wife Jolin Ellison, we shall see who invested more wisely. The guess here? Unfortunately, that opportunity comes against No. 18 Oregon inside Autzen Stadium, one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in college football. The Ducks will have the benefit of a hostile home crowd, while Michigan will be breaking in a new offensive coordinator and attempting to find some semblance of consistency on that side of the ball. It's hardly an ideal combination. When Michigan Has The Ball All eyes will be on interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding , who takes over following Kyle Whittingham's decision to fire Jason Beck. Michigan enters the matchup ranked No. 126 nationally in scoring offense, No. 109 in rushing offense, No. 125 in passing offense and No. 132 in total offense. Those numbers are remarkably poor for a program with Michigan's resources and expectations. Whittingham hasn't officially named freshman Tommy Carr the starter, but all signs point to No. 14 manning the offense. Carr has shown flashes since replacing Bryce Underwood, but he's also operating behind an offensive line that has struggled throughout the season. Against Oregon, those protection issues could become even more glaring. The Wolverines need Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter to establish something on the ground, particularly early. Otherwise, Carr could find himself facing obvious passing situations against an aggressive defense with the Autzen crowd making communication difficult. Harding doesn't need to reinvent the offense overnight. He needs to simplify things, establish manageable situations and give Carr opportunities to succeed. When Oregon Has The Ball Michigan's defense has been the more reliable unit by a mile, and that group will need another outstanding performance to keep this competitive. Defensive coordinator Jay Hill has enough talent to make things difficult, particularly with players like John Henry Daley, Zeke Berry, Chris Bracy and Jyaire Hill capable of creating disruptive plays. But Oregon presents a different challenge. The Ducks can put considerable pressure on a defense through tempo, athleticism, pure speed and offensive versatility. Michigan cannot afford repeated three-and-outs that force its defense to spend the afternoon on the field. If Oregon establishes an early lead, the Wolverines could find themselves in serious trouble. Michigan's defense should compete, but expecting Harding to completely transform one of America's worst offenses in less than a week is unrealistic. Autzen Stadium only makes matters worse. The Wolverines keep things respectable early before Oregon pulls away, leaving Michigan with two remaining opportunities to secure bowl eligibility. Oregon 27, Michigan 10

picks.headline: Oregon Predicted to Easily Handle Michigan This Week
picks.blurb: Oregon Predicted to Easily Handle Michigan This Week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Oregon Predicted to Easily Handle Michigan This Week (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODA) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:02 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in a good spot as the team enters the upcoming week of the college football season. Despite the Ducks having three losses on their resume, Oregon remains very much alive in the hunt for the College Football Playoff. In the new rankings for the playoff , Oregon came in ranked at No. 16, giving this team a real chance to get in. After taking down the Ohio State Buckeyes a week ago on the road, Oregon has put itself in a strong position to make some history. No team in the history of the playoff has reached the bracket with three losses, but this could be the year for it to happen. However, the Ducks will still need to win out for this to become any form of reality, and the team has three games left. First up for Oregon is a matchup at home against the Michigan Wolverines this weekend, with the Ducks feeling very confident heading into the game. With how the teams have played of late, Oregon is seen as the favorite to take down Michigan, giving this group more of a chance for the playoff. But the Ducks can't overlook the Wolverines, especially with their margin of error being so slim for the rest of the way. Bleacher Report's David Kenyon predicted the games of the week, including this matchup between Oregon and Michigan. In the prediction, Kenyon has the Ducks taking care of business against the Wolverines by a score of 28-13. Oregon starting quarterback Dante Moore is out for the rest of the year due to injury, and it's the Dylan Raiola show now. Raiola has given the Ducks some hope this season, providing a spark on offense. Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards with 11 touchdowns and two interceptions in seven games played for the Ducks this year. Losing Moore hurt this team, but Raiola has brought a sense of calm to the entire offense, giving them a chance to make some history. Against Michigan, Raiola will be called upon again, with him needing to put together a strong showing. The Wolverines can be a tricky team, with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr expected to get the start again this week. Carr has shown some ability to handle college defenses, but the Ducks can't take him lightly. If Oregon can take down Michigan, it would bring them that much closer to a playoff appearance.

Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Ryan Clarke · OregonLive.com Sat, November 14, 2026 at 6:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the best defenses Oregon will face all season comes into Autzen Stadium on Saturday, as the No. 16 Ducks play host to Michigan. The matchup has already featured some back-and-forth between the coaches, with Kyle Whittingham calling out Oregon's ability to "outbid everybody" for recruits and Dan Lanning responding in kind . But what happens between the lines, with Oregon seeking to make an unexpected run at the College Football Playoff and Michigan seeking to bounce back from a brutal loss to Michigan State? Here is a full preview: No. 16 Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) vs. Michigan (5-4, 2-4) When: Saturday, Nov. 14 Time: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene Latest line: Oregon by 10.5 points Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). If you are out of free trials, you can also watch this game with Sling (cheapest streaming plans that include live sports). Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. Three of Michigan's most important defensive players are listed as questionable as of Thursday evening: edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols, and safety Rod Moore Jr. That group has combined for 76 tackles this season including 8.5 sacks, and Moore is a crucial presence in the secondary. Oregon's offense is experiencing a resurgence, much of it due to an improved offensive line . Michigan playing without its two sack leaders would make a significant difference and perhaps allow the Ducks to break out for another big day. REPLACING A MAINSTAY Oregon has its own injury issues at the edge rusher spot: senior Teitum Tuioti is out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Ohio State, and the Ducks will have a tough time replacing both his production and leadership. One player who is set to see an uptick in snaps is the dynamic Nasir Wyatt, though he is listed as probable as of Thursday evening so he may be banged up. And Wyatt is a much different player than Tuioti, far more effective utilizing his speed as a pass-rusher than powering between the tackles and stopping the run. Others along Oregon's talented defensive line will need to fill the gaps and stop Michigan from running the ball effectively — a staple of Wolverine offenses past but something this iteration of Michigan has struggled with at times this season. QUARTERBACK CONTROVERSY Michigan is set to start Tommy Carr at quarterback on Saturday, but former five-star Bryce Underwood could see the field as well. The old saying is that if you have two quarterbacks, you don't have a quarterback, but Oregon has been in this situation before with Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Raiola has emerged from that low point and put together two excellent games in a row, seeking to keep the rhythm going on Saturday and continue to prove himself as Oregon's signal-caller for the long term. Michigan, however, is just hoping to have a somewhat effective game from one of its two struggling quarterbacks. Who that ends up being by the time the fourth quarter rolls around is certainly up in the air. Perhaps the Wolverines will experience the fired offensive coordinator bump, as Oregon has the past two games. Latest Ducks news What time is Oregon football vs. Michigan today? away.headline: Michigan State football’s good and bad injury updates before hosting Washington
away.blurb: The Spartans (3-6, 1-5 Big Ten) host Washington (5-4, 2-4) on Saturday (4:15 p.m., BTN) and standout defensive tackle Ben Roberts, cornerbacks Tre Bell and Charles Brantley and backup quarterback Cam Fancher were all upgraded to questionable after missing last week’s 15-6 win at Michigan. Michigan State’s first Big Ten-required availability report of the week released Wednesday night includes running back Jaziun Patterson as doubtful but there’s also the usual bad news the team has dealt with all season. There are 10 Spartans already ruled out against Washington, including safety and leading tackler Devin Vaught, top linebacker Jordan Hall, leading tight end Jayden Savoury, starting receiver Rodney Bullard and running back Marvis Parrish. The others, in addition to running back Cam Edwards being out for the season after a Week 4 injury, are safety Brayden Thomas, fullback Jay Coyne, offensive lineman Tristan Comer and tight end Joe Caudill. Hall, who has appeared in only four games, will miss his fourth in a row while Parrish is out for a second straight game and Bullard will miss his first. With Michigan State’s backfield depleted, Brandon Tullis stepped up to post career highs with 25 carries for 86 yards against the Wolverines. He appears poised to get more touches on Saturday. away.headline: Michigan football another underdog vs. UCLA, with a season-low point total
away.blurb: To little surprise, Michigan football will be another underdog when it returns home to play No. 4 UCLA this Saturday. Oddsmakers currently list the Wolverines as 5.5 to 6.5-point underdogs for the team’s final home game of the 2026 season (3:30 p.m., CBS). Numbers vary across the market, with BetMGM, DraftKings and Caesars currently showing Michigan +5.5, while FanDuel has Michigan +6.5. That number is smaller than Saturday’s game at Oregon, where the Wolverines opened as nearly two-touchdown underdogs before closing as 10-point underdogs. Michigan lost, 31-7, to the Ducks after another poor showing offensively. Michigan (5-5, 2-5 Big Ten) has failed to cover the spread in three straight games and six of its last seven, another sign of struggle for Kyle Whittingham’s team. As things stand currently, oddsmakers have also set a season-low point total for Saturday’s game, with books ranging from 37.5 to 39.5. Michigan’s had three games close with a total of 39.5 this season, including the last two. Eight of the Wolverines’ 10 games this season gave gone under the closing total, aided by Michigan’s 131st-ranked offense. Michigan’s opponent on Saturday, UCLA, is 10-0 under first-year coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins held off Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night to stay unbeaten, but it was the first time all season they failed to cover the spread. Yes, UCLA is 9-1 against the spread this season, overachieving expectations across the board, even from oddsmakers. Six of the Bruins’ 10 games have also gone under the total. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit mlive.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

home.headline: Oregon Ducks lose top running back for second straight week
home.blurb: Jordon Davison (leg) was listed as out on Wednesday’s availability report ahead of the No. 16 Ducks’ matchup with Michigan. But it’s not all bad news on offense: freshman wide receiver Messiah Hampton, who missed several games amid legal issues , is not listed on the report. Presumably that means he will be available on Saturday, though Dan Lanning hasn’t spoken on Hampton’s status for the remainder of the season. After a season-ending injury to star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti, the Ducks also saw his replacement — Nasir Wyatt — added to the report as probable with an undisclosed injury. Some key defensive players have a designation for Michigan as well: safety Rod Moore and star edge rusher John Henry Daley are both questionable. Oregon football will be without its top running back for the second consecutive week. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3) is back on the road this weekend, where it will meet the Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3) in Norman for a game that each side could really use in the win column. For Oklahoma, it won’t mean much in terms of a playoff push, but it will go a long way in salvaging what’s been a lost season. The Sooners don’t have consecutive wins (or losses) on the season yet, but they have collected wins over Texas and Florida in the last five weeks. For Ole Miss, its CFP hopes are on thin ice and to even be somewhat involved in the conversation next month, the Rebels badly need to win their final three regular season games. Ole Miss initially opened as a 2.5-point road favorite last week, but will now enter the weekend as a narrow 1.5-point underdog. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss On SI Staff Predictions Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) runs beside Ole Miss Rebels linebacker Suntarine Perkins (4) during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Ole Miss Rebels at Gaylord Family Ð Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis This weekend will mark another notable challenge for Ole Miss on the offensive side of the ball. It’s not an ideal weekend to not have Patrick Kutas available either, arguably Ole Miss’ top offensive lineman over the past two seasons. Oklahoma brings a defensive front that’s up to nearly 30 sacks on the year and one of the best run defenses in the conference, entering game day. Ole Miss desperately needs to bounce back in both departments, as it surrendered five sacks and ran for just 66 rushing yards in its loss last week. While there’s no doubt Ole Miss’ offensive line will get tested, and that Oklahoma will be sending consistent pressure, I’m picking Trinidad Chambliss to capitalize on what is looking like his final test against a great collegiate defense. Though Ole Miss will be without its leading tackler in Keaton Thomas, Oklahoma’s offense shouldn’t pose much of a threat anyway. It’s a golden opportunity for the Rebels to get right on that side of the ball. I expect a close game in Norman, thanks to the Sooners’ defense, but if one team was going to separate itself by multiple scores I think it would likely be Oklahoma. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 20 Matt Galatzan Ole Miss needs to get back on track if it is going to save its season. Fortunately, Oklahoma is the perfect opponent to do just that. The Sooners have struggled mightily this season, and the Rebels have the best quarterback in the country, and their backs against the wall. I think Ole Miss wins, and wins big. However, I have more faith in Ole Miss’ offense to recover from a string of poor performances, even if Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is out and Jason Witten has taken over as the Sooners’ interim offensive coordinator and play-caller. Give me the Rebels by three points in a game defined by the two teams’ defenses. Oklahoma’s defense is one of the toughest units in the SEC, and I expect Brent Venables to make life difficult for Trinidad Chambliss throughout the afternoon. However, I still have faith in Pete Golding’s defense to get the job done against an Oklahoma offense that is still trying to find its identity under Jason Witten. The Sooners looked better against Florida, but I need to see more before buying into the offensive turnaround. Ole Miss has too much at stake to let another opportunity slip away, and I expect Chambliss to lead a late scoring drive to secure a critical road victory. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Ole Miss' Trip to Oklahoma
picks.source: Ole Miss Rebels On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: No team should be judged by how they perform when everything is going its way, just as this Ole Miss program should be judged on how it can respond after the tumult it faced last time out against Georgia. With the Rebels' playoff hopes dwindling to the lowest they have been all season, Pete Golding's squad will need to respond in a big way this afternoon in Norman . Facing an Oklahoma team with a retooled offensive scheme and rejuvenated belief in itself, Ole Miss will need to capitalize on the trend that the Sooners have yet to win consecutive games this season. Just about everything went wrong at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last weekend for the Rebels, and it's true; everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. Golding's side took a clean hit to the jaw from the Bulldogs, and Ole Miss will need to claw itself up against Oklahoma if it wants a chance at getting back to the playoffs this season. Trinidad Chambliss Plays a Clean Game Following His Worst Showing Numbers talk, and for Trinidad Chambliss, they're quite damning. Throwing nine passes to the wrong side this season, the Rebels' former Heisman frontrunner is third in the Football Bowl Subdivision for interceptions this year. If Ole Miss wants to win on the road tomorrow and show that it can play in tough road environments, Chambliss will need to clean the turnovers up. The differences between Georgia and Oklahoma are clear, and I truly believe that Chambliss will return to the form he got fans used to in the 2025 season. The Rebels need their star to play a professional game today, and that all starts with taking care of the ball and making the right decisions when the Sooner pass rush gets in his way. The days of Chambliss and Kewan Lacy backfields are over this year, and the former will need to remind the Rebels' faithful of the leader he is capable of being. Behind a reworked offensive line, I expect Chambliss to erase the doubts that have been growing surrounding him recently, and #6 will lead Ole Miss to victory in Norman on the heels of a strong offensive showing. Shekai Mills-Knight has the Best Rushing Performance of the Season While Lacy's legacy in Oxford looks like it will end full of questions about injuries and unfulfilled potential, the Rebels have a tailback capable of reshaping the team's rushing narrative late in the season. I wholeheartedly believe in Ole Miss' French-Canadian sophomore, and John David Baker's offensive scheming needs to rely on the talent that can line up beside Chambliss. Shekai Mills-Knight, when utilized by Baker, has been a revelation for Ole Miss' rushing attack; the only issue is that Knight has been used nowhere near enough. Makhi Frazier has left a lot to be desired since arriving at Ole Miss from Michigan State, and with Knight receiving the leftover touches, the Rebels have seen what the sophomore back is capable of. If Shekai Mills-Knight is given an uptick in touches in Norman, there is no reason that the tailback cannot eclipse Ole Miss' single-game leading rusher this season: Kewan Lacy's 122-yard showing against Missouri. The Rebels need to be more dynamic offensively, and it all starts with feeding the Canadian native. The Defense Holds Oklahoma Under 21 Georgia's offense was able to do whatever it wanted in Oxford last weekend, and the Rebels will need to suffocate John Mateer and the Sooners under the new Jason Witten-led offense. Ole Miss has lived off of its offense for the past two seasons, and with how things have gone recently, a strong defensive showing in Norman will go a long way, not just towards a win but towards proving to the selection committee that the Rebels are worthy of making the postseason. Golding's defense has the talent to be great, now it just needs to translate to the field. The Rebels fell nine spots in this week’s CFP rankings, following its uncompetitive loss to Georgia, and no longer possess control of their postseason destiny. Ole Miss On SI's Tyler Komis and co-host Bailey Flanders dive into Ole Miss’ season up to this point and preview its game against Oklahoma this weekend. I think being defensive guys, you know what creates issues on defense alternative formations,” Golding said. “I think the defensive concepts of both defensive head coaches as well — it’s like, ‘okay, how do I shrink the game, number one, when you’re playing an explosive offense?’ That’s by controlling the football, being able to establish the run game, which both those guys believe in. I think being defensive guys, you know what creates issues on defense alternative formations,” Golding said. “I think you saw that with Florida. Last week there’s ten snaps of unbalance plus one run game. I think they’re getting the quarterback going in the run game as well to make you account for all 11. And then from a defensive standpoint create negative yardage plays (and are) very aggressive. Venables’ defense is very much like you saw on Saturday (against Georgia). You know that was probably one of their higher pressure games being Georgia. You know a lot of seven up looks and things like that.” “I think some of the post-snap RPO game has been eliminated a little bit. Some of that decision making process for the quarterback. They still have RPOs. I think a lot of them are pre-snap box generated based on numbers and free access and things like that. I think a lot of the run schemes are similar in the same way. I think they’re trying to get the quarterback’s legs going a little more than before. They’ve always had some quarterback designed runs, but it felt like that was more of an emphasis in the Florida game. Obviously (Jason) Witten being a tight end, the tight end’s going to be a piece of the package, and they’ve got some good tight ends,” Golding said of Oklahoma’s new interim offensive coordinator. “You know 81 is a really good player. But I think taking more off the quarterback you know as far as from a progression standpoint and reads post-snap and being a little more specific in the run game based on formation. A little more alternative with a shift and a motion, which has kind of been the theme against us anyway. So I think simplifying it within reason and then making you account for the quarterback.” Published Nov 13, 2026 TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Stuckey · Action Network Sun, November 15, 2026 at 2:09 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ole Miss Rebels take on the Oklahoma Sooners in Norman, Oklahoma, on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the weekend favored by 1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -104. But the Rebels didn't travel to Norman until Sunday, and now the Sooners are -2.5 favorites. The over/under sits at 48.5 total points. Here's my Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football pick for Sunday, November 15. Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Pick: Oklahoma -1 or Better My Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss best bet is on the Sooners. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Odds, Spread Lines Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Spread : Ole Miss +2.5, Oklahoma -2.5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Over/Under : 48.5 Total Points Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Moneyline : Ole Miss ML +120, Oklahoma ML -142 I couldn't have been more wrong about last week's playoff rematch between Ole Miss and Georgia. The Rebels got absolutely stomped from start to finish in every facet. Now, with three losses under their belts and only games against Mississippi State and Wofford remaining over the final two weeks, I don't see a path to the College Football Playoff, which the Ole Miss locker room is likely fully aware of. There's a reason you're hearing about season-ending injuries and the portal already in Oxford. Do they show up this week in Norman? It's certainly a question worth posing for a team that had national title aspirations. Even if Ole Miss is fully locked in during practice all week and shows up ready to roll on Saturday, I still would feel confident holding a Sooners ticket. Let's start with injuries, where these two teams are headed in opposite directions. The Rebels recently learned star running back Kewan Lacy will shut it down for the remainder of the season. Plus, they will have to make do this week without their best offensive lineman in Patrick Kutas and leading tackler in linebacker Keaton Thomas. Meanwhile, the Oklahoma offensive line is finally getting back to full strength. The biggest addition was getting starting left tackle Michael Fasusi back a few weeks ago. There was previously a massive void at left tackle, which has since been filled by the former five-star who finally looked 100% healthy last week at Florida. Not only will pass protection improve immensely, but the running game should continue to look more competent the rest of the season, especially against an Ole Miss defense that has plenty of holes against the run and pass. Last week also marked the debut of Oklahoma's new play-caller, Jason Witten. I thought he did a fantastic job with play sequencing, and the entire operation just looked cleaner. Most importantly, Oklahoma didn't have any turnovers, which have absolutely killed them all season. Witten also unleashed John Mateer with a higher rate of designed runs. It also helps that Mateer is finally playing with confidence. Earlier in the season, he could barely scramble without literally dropping the ball and was extremely hesitant to fire on his reads. It was as if he almost had the quarterback version of the yips. With that said, it's not like this offense is going to turn into the 1999 Rams. This is still a team that's led by an elite defense that should get constant pressure on Trinidad Chambliss, especially without Kutas and a backfield that struggles in picking up blitzes. Chambliss has really struggled against the last two top-tier defenses he faced in Texas and Georgia. This is just not the same offense as last year. Not only is Lacy done for the year, but there's a new play-caller, and the pass-catchers aren't as talented. As a result, Chambliss' efficiency numbers have fallen precipitously when under pressure. That could spell doom against a Brent Venables stop unit that generates pressure at one of the highest rates in the country. From a regression standpoint, don't be surprised if Oklahoma falls on a key fumble or two. The Sooners have the lowest fumble recovery rate in the country at 23%, while the Rebels rank 20th in that department at nearly 80%. This is not my typical buy-low / sell-high spot, as Ole Miss got blown out last week, while Oklahoma pulled off a road upset. However, I still think this sets up well for the Sooners, who are trending up offensively with a defense that should give Chambliss fits. And I do question whether or not we get a fully locked-in Rebels bunch this week. Pick: Oklahoma -1 or Better

picks.headline: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. Starting right guard Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among the 11 Rebels ruled out for Saturday's game. Franklin and Denson, meanwhile, remain uncertain after appearing on both availability reports this week. The next update is scheduled for Friday night, with final designations coming before Saturday's kickoff in Norman. away.headline: Kewan Lacy Injury Update, Latest on Ole Miss Star's Status, Return Timeline amid CFP Bracket Push
away.blurb: Lacy missed time with a shoulder injury earlier this season before suffering a dislocated shoulder in an Oct. 24 game at Texas. He had already been ruled out of Saturday's matchup at Oklahoma. The running back was listed as the No. 21 prospect on Bleacher Report's 2027 NFL draft big board back in September. Lacy is eligible to either enter the draft or return for another college season in 2027. Saturday will mark Lacy's third straight absence. He will also be expected to sit out an Oct. 21 matchup against Wofford and the Oct. 27 regular-season finale against Mississippi State. Bleacher Report • 15h Hutchinson Out For Season Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss will have to continue their push for the College Football Playoff without star running back Kewan Lacy. On3's Pete Nakos reported Thursday Lacy is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to injury. Scouts have only gotten to see Lacy play the majority of a single college season. After appearing in six games as a true freshman at Missouri, Lacy joined Ole Miss in 2025 and went on to lead the FBS with 306 carries. Lacy paced the SEC with 24 rushing touchdowns during that sophomore season to go with 1,567 rushing yards over 15 games. Injuries have kept Lacy from replicating that campaign as a junior. He will finish the 2026 season with 78 carries for 388 yards and five scores. Lacy's injury issues started when he suffered what Ole Miss coach Pete Golding called a "bruised" left shoulder last December during a first-round CFP win over Tulane. home.blurb: Ole Miss listed Chambliss as probable for Saturday in the initial SEC availability report , putting the Rebels' starting quarterback on track to play. However, the Rebels didn't detail the injury, and Chambliss didn't show issues in last weekend's game. That makes Chambliss' probable designation significant for an Ole Miss team attempting to recover from its worst offensive performance of the season. The Rebels managed only seven points in Saturday's 42-7 loss to Georgia, falling to 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play. Depending on Chambliss' status, the Rebels could fall off of the College Football Playoff run entirely — they are ranked No. 19 in the latest CFP rankings — and put an early, virtual end to their season. Chambliss completed 18 of 34 passes for 170 yards against the Bulldogs but failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season. The Kentucky Wildcats look to bounce back from last week's brutal loss at Tennessee when they host the rival Florida Gators on Saturday night. My Florida vs Kentucky prop picks feature two Wildcats who should thrive against the Gators' struggling defense, plus a Florida quarterback who could benefit from a pass-heavy game script. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Florida vs Kentucky predictions ahead of kickoff at 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Best Florida vs Kentucky props Prop pick #1: CJ Baxter Over 63.5 rushing yards Kentucky's offense has rolled when it hasn't faced a high-caliber defense this season, and Florida certainly doesn't qualify. I'm backing CJ Baxter to have himself a day, and I'd play this rushing total up to 56% against a Florida front that ranks among the nation's worst in stuff rate . The Gators rank in the bottom half nationally in explosive run rate allowed, a key reason they're 93rd in EPA per rush and 111th in success rate. The Wildcats rank third in success rate this year and sit in the 83rd percentile in explosive run rate. Baxter's 38.8% breakaway yard rate ranks 29th among 116 backs with at least 90 carries. With a game script that should see him get 15-plus carries, this one's a no-brainer for me. Prop pick #2: Willie Rodriguez Over 48.5 receiving yards Florida's defense allowed Oklahoma tight end Rocky Beers to rack up 72 yards on just four catches last week, his best game since September. That's why I'm backing Willie Rodriguez for a strong outing, playable up to 55%. Rodriguez ranks second on the Wildcats in targets. In Will Stein's offense, quarterback Kenny Minchey has been taught to take what's given to him, and the tight end has become a reliable option. Brad White's soft zone defense ranks 120th in defensive passing success rate and sits in the 18th percentile in explosive pass rate. Rodriguez ranks sixth among all tight ends in yards after catch (YAC). He's caught at least five passes in six of Kentucky's seven SEC games, and that consistent volume makes this receiving total very attainable. Prop pick #3: Aaron Philo Over 194.5 passing yards Sources have confirmed that Aaron Philo will start at quarterback for Florida this week, and I'm backing him to clear this total, playable up to 54%. I don't think Philo will have a good game overall, as the Wildcats should get after him and pick him off at least once. But this Kentucky defense is prone to giving up big plays through the air and struggles to get off the field on third down, ranking 132nd in yards to gain and 115th in success rate. The Gators rank 29th in passing success rate , and they're often forced into passing situations because of the ridiculous number of penalties committed by their offensive line. Philo surpassed this number in all six of his starts before the Georgia game. With Kentucky expected to play from ahead, Philo should have enough passing opportunities to do so again, provided Jon Sumrall doesn't pull him.
