picks.blurb: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers 49ers outgun Cowboys Fantasy Booms and Busts Aidan Hutchinson injury College football winners/losers Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will Stein's Kentucky football team hosts Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators team under the lights at Kroger Field tomorrow at 6:15 P.M. ET. Florida has came back down to earth after a strong September and Kentucky is looking to bounce back after suffering their second loss of the season. We preview the Gators offense and defense, as well as laid out the path to victory for the Wildcats. Now, I will give my final thoughts on the matchup and a prediction for the game. Coach Stein said that last week was only the second time in his coaching career that his offense failed to score a touchdown. This team and the offense specifically will be looking to make a statement tomorrow night. They will get a perfect opportunity against a Brad White defense that has struggled all season for the Gators. As we know from watching years of Brad White's scheme in Lexington, they love to play soft zone coverage and allow easy completions to offenses in hopes of executing a bend-don't-break style of defense. The big advantage is this Kentucky offense is built off of efficiency and getting Kenny Minchey easy completions in quick game. This creates an advantageous scheme matchup for Will Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. If the Wildcats can eliminate the self-inflicted mistakes from last week in Knoxville, you have to like their chances to put together long scoring drives. The difference in this game being close and the Cats running away with it is if the offense can start to find the explosive plays. One area of this matchup we have not talked about is the weather aspect of this football game on Saturday. The past few days in Lexington have turned extremely cold, and temperatures for kickoff at looking at 40 degrees or below. Combine that with the winds, it will be freezing at Kroger Field and will only get colder as the game goes on. You have to wonder how this Florida team will respond in these conditions especially if they don't start fast in this one. This Florida team is reeling, they have lost four of their last five games. The drop-off has been eye-opening for the Gators because they looked like one of the best teams in the country through the first month of the season. Defenses have figured out how to bottle up their run game and the offense has started to suffer because of it. The Gators offense led them to their hot start to the Jon Sumrall era and covered up the rough play on the defensive side of the football. Kentucky has to stop this rushing attack and get Florida into a dropback heavy game. The Gators are going back to Aaron Philo after starting Tramell Jones last week. The old saying goes: if you have two quarterbacks, you have none. I think the Wildcats will be prepared to potentially see both guys this week as the Gators will try everything they can to generate some offense. Florida has to answer questions offensively, their offensive line is one of the worst in the conference and the quarterback situation is not ideal. Brad White has not figured out how to fix the Gators defensive issues in his first year away from Lexington. I think Kentucky capitalizes on that and has one of their best offensive performances of the season following last week where they failed to reach the end zone. Kentucky has their backs against the wall, they will make the College Football Playoff if they win the last three games and I believe the offense makes a statement in the cold at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 38, Florida 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction

Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they'll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their mind, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone's guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Florida Gators Location: Kroger Field- Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 14th Time: 6:15 PM ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel Sportsbook has Kentucky favored by 3.5 points with an over/under of 51.5. ESPN win probability: ESPN FPI gives Kentucky a 54% chance of victory Our prediction I'm not going to lie, this game has got weirdness written all over it. Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6'6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side of Kentucky's line, which struggled down in Knoxville. Ultimately, I think Kentucky does clean it up, and despite some pressure off the edge, the Cats knock off the Gators. away.headline: Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky
away.blurb: GAINESVILLE, Fla. — The Florida Gators are making yet another change at quarterback. Aaron Philo, who had been benched for last week’s loss to Oklahoma , will return as the starter for this week’s game at Kentucky. CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz was first to report. The decision is the latest in a series of moves at the position between Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., as struggles at the position have mounted over the last month. Philo was replaced by Jones Jr. in losses to Missouri and South Carolina before missing the Texas game with an injury. Jones Jr. threw for two touchdowns in that start and replaced Philo after three drives, two weeks later in the loss to Georgia. Last week’s loss to the Sooners was a negative turning point for the true sophomore, though, with Jones Jr. completing just 10 of his 22 passes for 133 yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions. He played all but one offensive snap, with Philo coming in for a handoff for just one play. “Think both guys have done some really good things this year at times, and both guys have done some not-so-good things at times,” head coach Jon Sumrall said on Monday. “Didn't think we played well enough at quarterback on Saturday.” Jones Jr. is also dealing with an undisclosed injury that Sumrall said could require surgery in the offseason. However, Jones Jr. said after the loss that the injury is not holding him back. Florida’s recent struggles at the position — a microcosm of other issues on the offensive line, injury issues at receiver, and difficulties in the run game with the running backs — have led to outside discussions on the long-term status of the position and both Philo’s and Jones Jr.’s individual futures with the program. Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said the team’s focus remains on developing those currently on the roster and not looking towards the NCAA Transfer Portal to address the position. “We got three games to evaluate everything,” he said. “Look, one thing about me is if I tell you, like, I do believe in them. And I do understand that it is a process with the quarterback position, and I will not rush that process, right? I want to stand by those guys. I'm gonna bring them along. It's our job to coach them.” Kickoff on Saturday between Florida and Kentucky is at 6:15 p.m., with television coverage on ESPN. Have the Florida Gators Reopened its Quarterback Battle? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The Wildcats will try to spoil the Utes' perfect season in a ranked battle Big 12 battle Getty Images Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications . The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. The game was originally scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET primetime slot on Saturday, but due to travel issues caused by the FAA shutdown on Friday , kickoff was moved to 10:30 p.m. for this pivotal showdown. Where to watch Utah vs. Arizona live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 10:30 p.m. ET Location : Casino Del Sol Stadium -- Tucson, Arizona TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: "The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team's biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He's allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He's an extremely competitive coach, but he's able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop." Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? "Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It's giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he's been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn't have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing." Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? "Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah's offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he's really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does." Arizona's secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? "The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size." How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona's passing attack? "Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it's likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him." Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we're seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? "The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people's person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It's not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it's a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He's also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it's just complaining, though he'd listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team." Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. "This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it's far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year's past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they've got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 ."

picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football vs. Utah Utes score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 16, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Twice this season, Arizona has found itself up against a ranked opponent with a chance to make a big splash on the national stage, and both times it led at halftime only to fall in the end. Third time’s a charm? No. 22 Arizona (7-2, 4-2) plays its biggest game of the year on Saturday, hosting unbeaten No. 2 Utah (9-0, 6-0) with a chance to climb back into the Big 12 title race and the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. How will the Wildcats do in this Top 25 clash? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Utah wins 30-28 Utah is not a team that has difficulty scoring. The Utes average 34.3 points per game against their FBS opponents this season. Their lowest output was 21 points against Houston. They’ve only been held below 30 points by three of their FBS opponents: Houston, BYU, and (surprisingly) Colorado. Arizona will be Utah’s third ranked opponent but first on the road. Will it matter that the game isn’t in Salt Lake City? Doubtful. The Wildcats had issues with mobile quarterbacks. While Arizona is ranked fifth in the Big 12 with 203.3 pashing yards allowed per game, Devon Dampier doesn’t just rely on his arm to move the ball. He throws for 228.1 ypg. He’s also second on the team in rushing with 53.6 ypg on the ground. Dampier is going to be playing in his home state against his former head coach. The now-assistant coach at Arizona admits that he should have played Dampier more when they were both at New Mexico. The senior from Phoenix may have something to prove and a group of friends and family members in attendance to prove it to. On the positive side, Arizona should be able to move the ball, too. Utah is ninth in the Big 12 in passing yards allowed at 233.8 per game. Noah Fifita is fourth in the nation in passing yards per game (310.4), total passing yards (2,794), and total offense per game (325.4). The Arizona defense has been solid for most of the year, but it barely kept the Big 12’s 15 th -ranked scoring offense under 30 points last week. Utah is the No. 2 scoring offense in the league. The Wildcats are No. 6. To make matters worse for the ‘Cats, Utah has the No. 2 scoring defense in the Big 12. Arizona’s in No. 5. With some luck, this one could be close. It would be a shocker to see Arizona pull off the upset, though. Ezra Amacher — Utah wins 27-24 Utah’s Devon Dampier is the type of quarterback that gives Arizona defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales cold sweats at night. The senior from Saguaro High School in Phoenix has grown into one of top dual-threat quarterbacks in the country. He ranks second among all active FBS quarterbacks with 2,811 career rushing yards. He has a dang good arm as well and doesn’t commit many turnovers. Arizona struggled to stop the other dual-threat QBs it faced this year in TCU’s Jaden Craig and West Virginia’s Michael Hawkins Jr. Dampier is better than either of them and has a stalwart offensive line protecting him. I don’t see the Wildcats defense being able to do enough to keep Utah off the board. That wouldn’t be as much of a concern against a lesser opponent, but Utah’s defense is outstanding. The Utes give up 16.3 points per game, second-fewest in the Big 12. They’re riding high on confidence after forcing BYU’s Bear Bachmeier into four interceptions last week. I give Utah the edge. Adam Green — Arizona wins 31 -27 Why the hell not. Here in this space is where I try to convince you all (and myself, really) that this pick is an actual prediction rather than wischasting. So here we go. Arizona is good — very good — at home. Utah has not beaten a ranked team on the road. Arizona has everything to play for and is coming off a victory that likely served as a wake up call while inspiring confidence. Utah, on the other hand, has a little bit of breathing room and is coming off an emotional and physical victory over rival BYU. Finally, Arizona has Noah Fifita . The QB is a perfect 2-0 against Morgan Scalley’s defense, with the most recent victory coming in Salt Lake City during a season in which the Wildcats were not a particularly good team. That Fifita is playing the best football of his career heading into this game and has weapons like Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson is nothing to feel bad about. This isn’t to say that it will be an easy game like the last time these teams played in Tucson, because it’s hard to imagine No. 2 in the nation going down without a fight. Utah’s offense is going to be more dynamic than we’re used to seeing but their defense is gettable for an Arizona team that is quite capable of slinging the ball around. Keep penalties to a minimum and win the turnover battle, and Arizona will win the game. Juan Serrano — Arizona wins 31-28 Arizona is a different team when it plays inside Casino Del Sol Stadium. Of course, last week’s game was a miracle and not usually how the Wildcats play at home. The defense did only surrendered 21 points to TCU which is usually a winning formula. Noah Fifita ’s pick-six was a rarity and kept the Horned Frogs in the game. He cannot afford to have those type of plays against Utah, and I don’t think he will. Fifita usually has some of his best games against the Utes. I also think Arizona missed two shots at a big win against BYU and Texas Tech. It’s time for the ball to bounce in the way of the Wildcats in terms of making a statement. Utah has only been favored by 2.5 since the end of the Holy War, and it has stuck there. That is a very good sign for Arizona. Devon Dampier does present a big issue for the defense but I would not be surprised if Danny Gonzales presents a different picture for Dampier. He knows his defense has struggled against mobile quarterbacks and it has shown in many games. Something will need to change schematically for the Wildcats to have a chance to win. It all comes down to what is at stake for Arizona. This is a season defining, program defining moment for Brent Brennan ’s squad. The home winning streak will continue for the Wildcats and will earn one of the most historic wins in Arizona football history. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 30-24 I’m not going to lie, I’ve been tossing this one back and forth in my mind. The Wildcats at home are a force to be reckoned with. I throw out the issues from Arizona last week as kind of fluky. They were coming off an emotional loss against Texas Tech, and on a short week no less. Noah Fifita’s rare and odd pick six, Dwight Bootle’s rough night and the not-great tackling were all things that caused the closeness of the game against TCU. On the other side, you have Utah coming off an physical and emotional Holy War win against BYU last week. As of this writing, Utah looks like they’ll be without their leader in sacks, DL Karson Kaufusi , who has 3 sacks this year. However, the Utes still have Jireh Moe and Elijah Elliss , who are also fantastic d-linemen and have combined for 62 tackles, 9.5 TFLs and 5 sacks. Overall, this game is going to come down to QB play. Not breaking any news here, but Noah is a stud and will have to play a near flawless game. If he plays his game and doesn’t force anything, or make any plays like last week’s pick six, Arizona has a legit chance to win. For the Utes, Devon Dampier is a problem. He has been effective through the air this season, however, his legs are his biggest strength. He is a fantastic runner and is Utah’s second leading rusher. Even if he doesn’t gain massive yards, he is able to extend plays and forces the defense to respect his running ability. Finally, I think Danny Gonzales will change some things up for Utah. I don’t expect to see the same looks that TCU got, mainly due to the injuries on defense. I believe Danny has learned from the Tommy Castellanos issues and won’t make it as easy for Dampier. Couple that with slowing down Wayshawn Parker and playing in front of what seems to be turning into a packed Sol, I think the defense can do it. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 21-20 As I wrote earlier this week , November has traditionally been the month when Arizona has picked up its biggest home wins. It’s been a while, though, and most of those have been when the Wildcats are a decided underdog and the game isn’t in the national spotlight. Not the case this time, with a very small spread and Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff is in town. The losses at BYU and Texas Tech had a common theme beyond leading at halftime. Both saw the UA struggle mightily in the second half, scoring only nine total points, though each time it was down four and driving with a chance to go back in front. One missed play turned everything. Utah is a very good team with no weakness, and has the kind of dual-threat weapon in Devon Dampier that Arizona traditionally struggles with. But it’s November, and strange things happen at night in the desert. picks.blurb: Brian Kelly's Official Prediction for Texas-LSU Matchup Might Surprise You Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB Former LSU Tigers head coach Brian Kelly believes Lane Kiffin's squad will pick up the win in Week 11 when the Texas Longhorns travel to Baton Rouge for a battle under the lights. He made his official prediction with CBS Sports this week. Kelly doesn't believe the Longhorns' offensive line will be up to the task of protecting quarterback Arch Manning against an elite LSU pass rush. "I've always felt that by the 10th week of the season, you are who you are. And I think those things will show with Texas and the inability to protect the quarterback. I worry about that," Kelly said about Texas's protection on CBS Sports airwaves . "For LSU, it's situational offense in particular. They were 0-for-4 on fourth down (against Alabama last week), and they were abysmal in the red zone. But I think you can fix those things, so I'm leaning toward LSU making the adjustments that they need to and winning the football game." Some fans might have expected Kelly to pick Texas for a few reasons. For starters, the Longhorns have a better collection of wins and are on a three-game winning streak. But on top of that, the narrative is that Kelly had some sort of grudge against LSU and will look to pick against them at every turn. However, Kelly's comments make it clear that he's confident in what LSU brings to the table in this matchup. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB The trouble with bold predictions is they tend to sound a little ridiculous — right up until they happen. There are plenty of reasonable expectations for Saturday night’s matchup between Texas and LSU. But reasonable expectations aren’t all that interesting, are they? So let’s throw a little caution to the wind. Maybe these predictions will look brilliant by the final whistle. Maybe they’ll be aging poorly before halftime. But that’s half the fun in the first place. Here are three bold predictions for the Longhorns’ trip to Baton Rouge. Raleek Brown Rushes for Over 100 Yards Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, Missouri, USA; Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown runs the ball during the first half against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. William Purnell-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. LSU enters Saturday allowing just 84.7 rushing yards per game, the second-best mark in the SEC. Meanwhile Texas has struggled to establish consistency on the ground for much of the season. But if there’s a Longhorn capable of bucking that trend, it’s Raleek Brown. Against Ole Miss, Brown demonstrated what an elite Texas run game could look like given the opportunity, carrying the ball 23 times for 157 yards. Last weekend, he once again flashed that potential, rushing for 85 yards on 17 attempts. With Sarkisian emphasizing the importance of avoiding situations where Texas falls behind the chains, establishing the run game early will likely be a priority. That could mean a concerted effort to feed Brown from the opening drive, allowing him to find his rhythm. It certainly won't be easy against an LSU defensive front that has made life miserable for opposing running backs all season. But if Sarkisian can get Brown going, don't be surprised if he eclipses the century mark. Colin Simmons Records Three Sacks Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons in action during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Before his ankle injury, it would’ve been fair to argue that Colin Simmons was the best defensive player in the nation. Through his first six games, the junior accumulated 10.5 sacks — a metric he still leads the SEC in despite missing more than 2 games — and 16 tackles for loss. After playing just 18 snaps against Missouri, Simmons has yet to fully establish himself as the disruptive force that terrorized opposing offenses earlier in the season. Saturday might change that. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was sacked four times against Alabama last weekend, and Texas’ defensive front will prove to be another difficult assignment. But perhaps the most intriguing aspect of this prediction is Leavitt’s style of play. Leavitt has demonstrated a willingness to escape the pocket and improvise when plays begin to break down, often extending plays with his legs in hopes of creating something out of nothing. And while that ability makes him a dangerous dual-threat quarterback, it could also present an opportunity for a player with Simmons’ speed and relentless pursuit. Simmons doesn't necessarily need to beat his blocker immediately to disrupt a play. His closing speed allows him to pursue quarterbacks well after they've escaped the initial pressure, potentially turning Leavitt's improvisation into opportunities for sacks. Yes, three sacks is asking a lot, especially from a player still working his way back from an ankle injury. But if Simmons is even close to full strength, there's little reason to believe he can't once again take over a game. Texas Forces Three Turnovers Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt looks to pass the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nine interceptions in nine games. Nine interceptions in nine games. That’s the rather alarming statistic surrounding Leavitt , even if those numbers don’t necessarily tell the full story. Not all nine interceptions have been his fault. But Leavitt has shown a tendency to misread defenders dropping into coverage and force throws into crowded windows, mistakes that Texas could be well-positioned to exploit. The Tigers have committed 13 turnovers this season, including four lost fumbles. And while Texas has forced just 10 turnovers through nine games, with Simmons healthy, Rasheem Biles playing some of his best football and a secondary capable of capitalizing on hurried throws, the Longhorns have all the pieces to give Texcalibur quite the night. away.blurb: For No. 8 Texas (8-2, 5-2), the dreams of the playoffs continue while LSU will look to still get the taste of defeat out of its mouth as it hits the road next week to face No. 9 Tennessee at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 21 inside Neyland Stadium in Knoxville. Longhorns have the ball but if you're an LSU fan, your defense is the unit you want on the field to try and close this game out. Tigers have limited Texas to just 217 yards of offense and have forced three turnovers. Slowly but surely, Texas is getting back into this game as Gianni Spetic knocks in his third field goal of the game. He knocked this one in from 50 yards out to shrink LSU's lead to just five points. The Tigers have been living and dying in the air for the most part of this game until running back Dillin Jones found a lane. Jones broke out for a 44-yard rushing touchdown to extend LSU's lead. The run marks the longest rush of the night so far as both teams haven't run it a ton with success. That last possession of the half for LSU was a dud. Once the offense got close to the end zone, Texas' defense bowed up and LSU fizzled out. Leavitt just lobbed that ball up. I know the pressure is in his face but he's got to rifle that ball out of the back of the end zone. LSU OC Charlies Weis Jr. had Leavitt roll out plenty to avoid Texas' army of pass rushers. Get used to seeing that a lot tonight. After falling to Alabama last Saturday and suffering its third loss on the 2026 season, LSU couldn’t afford to lose against Texas inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With their backs against the wall Lane Kiffin and his Tigers (6-4, 3-4 SEC) battled for every point while also trying to neutralize Texas’ star quarterback Arch Manning. In the end, Manning pulled off the second half heroics to help the Longhorns storm back and beat LSU 22-21. Thus ending the Tigers dream of making it to the College Football Playoff. It was far from pretty on offense for the Tigers. Quarterback Sam Leavitt matched his season-high in interceptions, throwing three. Interceptions were the theme of the night, with both Leavitt and Manning combining for six picks. Despite it, Manning and company only needed the final two minutes to go right as he finished the night throwing for 174 yards and a 4-yard game-winning touchdown. Defensively, LSU held the Longhorns to a season-low in points as they brought pressure almost every snap, making it hard for Manning to do what he does best; use he’s legs and pick defenses apart.
